Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our demo focused on logging and redaction: 

Summary of ask:
- FintechCo needs assurance that request/response logs, headers, and trace IDs will not leak PII (card numbers, account IDs, SSNs).
- You asked about retention windows, ability to disable request/response logs per route, and support for data residency in us-east-1.
- Security team requested an overview of redaction tooling and an example masking configuration.

What Redwood can provide (high-level):
- Configurable logging profiles per-route: full, metadata-only, or disabled. Metadata-only stores only routing/telemetry (latency, token counts) and drops request/response payloads.
- Automatic sensitive-field redaction at ingress: configurable regex and schema-based redaction for headers and JSON bodies, with hashing option for identifiers (one-way HMAC).
- Trace ID handling: trace IDs can be canonicalized and stored separately (no payload correlation) or suppressed entirely from logs.
- Retention and residency: retention windows are configurable per-customer; we support region pinning (us-east-1, eu-west-1).

Attachments: I attached a short "redwood-logging-controls.pdf" and an example masking YAML that shows the config we discussed. Also attached our SOC 2 summary for context.

2) We’ll provide a sandbox checklist and a sample config you can run against a dev endpoint.
3) If that looks good, we’ll provide formal language for your procurement team/contract (retention/residency SLA).

Please confirm the time that works or suggest alternatives.

Alex/Samantha —

Great questions — answered inline and looping in Aditya and Vivek for the technical details: 

1) Server-side redaction: Redwood performs redaction at the ingress proxy layer, before any request/response payloads are written to persistent storage. The pipeline order is: TLS termination -> ingress parsing and schema-based redaction -> routing -> runtime. Redaction is enforced in-memory and verified by our persistence layer to reject any accidental writes containing configured-sensitive fields.

2) Default coverage and schema-driven rules: Out of the box we block common PAN patterns (Luhn check), SSNs (regex), and a set of header keys. For anything custom (internal account_id, proprietary identifiers), you can upload a JSON schema or provide a list of keys/regex; our masking engine will generate rules and we can test them in your sandbox. The attached "example-masking-config.yaml" shows auto-generated rules for an "account_id" field.

3) Hashing and forensics: We support two modes:
- One-way hashing (HMAC with customer salt) for correlation where forensics isn't required.
- Customer-managed escrow keys: for customers that need reversible pseudonymization under strict controls, we integrate with KMS/HSM so decryption requires an auditable key-retrieval process and multi-party approval. We will include this in the deep-dive.

4) Retention policy examples: see attached excerpt in the PDF. Short answer: metadata-only mode keeps telemetry indefinitely (or per SLA) while removing request/response payloads after the configured TTL. I included a sample config for 30d vs 90d that shows request bodies are purged at TTL and only aggregated usage metrics remain.

Aditya/Vivek — could you bring the ingress sequence diagram and a short checklist of control-plane checks we run during persistence to the call?

Hi Alex/Samantha —

Quick technical notes ahead of today’s call: 

- Ingress redaction is implemented in the edge proxy (written in Rust), and redaction rules are compiled into a VM-safe trie for low-latency matching. That means rules run at <1ms additional latency in typical workloads.
- For PAN detection we run a multi-step heuristic: pattern match + Luhn + context (header/body field name). Hits are redacted to "<REDACTED-PAN>" unless you request hashing.
- Trace ID handling: by default we scrub trace IDs from stored logs; if you enable correlation we store a separate correlation table that contains only the hashed identifier and routing metadata (no payload).
- For escrowed reversible encryption we can integrate with your KMS; key access is logged and gated.

I attached a short example masking config and an ingress sequence diagram to the shared Drive link Marissa included. I’ll present these on the call.

Looking forward to it.
